bugs.error_message: User: 'Set Up Sharing hangs on the spinning icon, unable to press Done'; share was actually created (visible after force-quit)
bugs.root_cause: NSPersistentCloudKitContainer.share(_:to:) does blocking work on its calling thread, and under SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY (nonisolated(nonsending) caller's-actor semantics) the awaited async import ran it ON the main actor — freezing UI and deadlocking against completion delivery. Server record was created before the deadlock, hence post-restart visibility.
bugs.fix: createShare now wraps the completion-handler share(_:to:completion:) and persistUpdatedShare(_:in:completion:) in Task.detached + withCheckedThrowingContinuation, so all container work happens off the main actor; only the @Published share assignment returns to main.

bugs.error_message: User: after Stop Sharing, reopening the Household sheet shows sharing active again; correct only after app restart
bugs.root_cause: fetchShares(matching:) reads the LOCAL share cache, which keeps the deleted CKShare until the next mirroring import. Each sheet presentation created a fresh @StateObject SharingController that trusted the stale cache.
bugs.fix: SharingController is now a session singleton (SharingController.shared, @ObservedObject in HouseholdView) and tracks deletedShareRecordIDs; loadShare treats any cached share whose recordID is in that set as gone. stopSharing and leaveHousehold both record the deleted ID.

bugs.error_message: Release-config warnings: 'call to main actor-isolated static method normalize in a synchronous nonisolated context' (CategoryClassifier x2) + weak/strong capture warning in SharingController observer
bugs.root_cause: nonisolated on a class declaration does NOT extend to members declared in its extensions — they get the project's MainActor default, so GroceryItem.normalize was MainActor while its callers (nonisolated CategoryClassifier) were not. Swift 5 mode made it a warning, but it's an error in Swift 6 mode and a latent misisolation. The observer closure also implicitly strong-captured self alongside an inner weak capture (retain until observer removal).
bugs.fix: Marked normalize and foldTrailingPlural explicitly nonisolated; observer closure now [weak self] with early unwrap to a local strong ref passed into the MainActor Task. Release device build now has zero warnings. Note: [self] capture-list + implicit member refs does NOT satisfy 'explicit use of self' in Swift 5 mode — use a named local instead.

bugs.error_message: Unit tests crashed: 'CoreData: error: +[Household entity] Failed to find a unique match for an NSEntityDescription to a managed object subclass', then 'libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type NSException'
bugs.root_cause: NSPersistentCloudKitContainer(name:) loads a FRESH NSManagedObjectModel per instance. Each unit test builds its own in-memory PersistenceController, so N models declaring the same entities were loaded at once and Core Data could no longer map an entity name to its NSManagedObject subclass. Single-container apps never hit this; a second stack (previews + app, or one per test) does.
bugs.fix: Load the model exactly once into a static `managedObjectModel` (Bundle(for: GroceryItem.self) -> XWaste.momd) and pass it to NSPersistentCloudKitContainer(name:managedObjectModel:).

bugs.error_message: Watch XCUITest: tapping the check-off button on a shopping-list row opened the quantity screen instead. Accessibility dump after the tap showed quantity-value/quantity-increment, no check-off confirmation.
bugs.root_cause: On watchOS a NavigationLink placed inside a List row claims the WHOLE row's tap, so the sibling check-off Button never receives it. This violates the watch-app spec scenario 'Quantity controls do not steal the check-off tap'.
bugs.fix: Removed the row-level NavigationLink. The quantity control is now a plain Button that sets @State quantityItemID; the list pushes via .navigationDestination(item:). Decrement-to-zero reports back through an onRemoved closure so the list owns the confirmation (the detail view's own item is deleted by then).

bugs.error_message: macOS: after removing a row from the shopping list (delete OR check-off), surviving rows redraw with a neighbour's content - a section header rendered inside a row slot, and the remaining item vanished from view. Data was correct; only the rendering was wrong. Persisted across tab switches.
bugs.root_cause: SwiftUI's AppKit-backed List mis-diffs a row removal out of a MULTI-SECTION List: the row count updates correctly but content is drawn from the wrong index. PRE-EXISTING since v1 (reproduces via the v1 check-off path) - it was simply never seen because nobody ran the Mac build. Ruled out as causes: List(selection:), .onDeleteCommand, FetchRequest animation, and the Section(_:) vs Section{}header:{} form - all still reproduced.
bugs.fix: macOS-only `.id(structureID)` on the List, where structureID is the ordered join of every row's objectID URI. Any insertion/removal changes it and rebuilds the list, sidestepping the bad diff; quantity edits don't change it, so in-place updates still animate. iOS keeps its animated diffing.

bugs.error_message: macOS: the app launched at its MINIMUM width, not its .defaultSize, so the toolbar's Household and Add buttons were collapsed into an overflow chevron on every launch.
bugs.root_cause: `.frame(minWidth:minHeight:)` on the root view supplies the window's ideal size when no idealWidth/idealHeight is given, so SwiftUI sized the window to the minimum and `.defaultSize` never applied. At 380pt the toolbar cannot fit traffic lights + Household + tab picker + Add.
bugs.fix: Raised the floor to `.frame(minWidth: 480, idealWidth: 480, minHeight: 520, idealHeight: 720)`. 480pt is the measured width at which the whole toolbar fits with no overflow.

bugs.error_message: iPhone Watch app: 'This app could not be installed at this time.' when installing xwaste onto a physical Apple Watch.
bugs.root_cause: The watch target had NO asset catalog and no ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME, so the built bundle contained no Assets.car and no CFBundleIconName. watchOS refuses to install an app without an app icon on a PHYSICAL device; the simulator does not care, so all 10 watch XCUITests passed and every simulator build succeeded while the device install was impossible.
bugs.fix: Added xwaste-watch/Assets.xcassets with a watchOS AppIcon.appiconset (single 1024x1024, platform 'watchos') reusing the iOS icon PNG, and set ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME = AppIcon on both watch build configs. Verified the built bundle now has Assets.car containing AppIcon and Info.plist CFBundleIcons.CFBundleIconName = AppIcon.

bugs.error_message: Apple Watch showed 'Nothing to buy' on a fresh install while the paired iPhone showed a full list, on the same iCloud account and same CloudKit environment.
bugs.root_cause: resolveActiveHousehold() runs at launch when a fresh install's local store is still empty. Finding no Household it CREATES one and persists its id as active. CloudKit then imports the real household and its items, but activeHousehold stays pinned to the invented empty one, and every fetch is scoped to it - so the device shows an empty list forever while the synced data sits unreachable in the same store. It also leaves a stray empty Household in the user's private CloudKit database. Latent since v1; impossible to hit on a single device, which is exactly why deferred task 10.1 (same-account second-device sync) never caught it.
bugs.fix: Track activeHouseholdWasAutoCreated (persisted across launches, since the first import often lands after a relaunch). While that flag is set, adoptSyncedHouseholdIfPresent() switches to the earliest other household as soon as one arrives, deletes the invented empty one, and clears the flag. Runs at init and on every .NSPersistentStoreRemoteChange. Guards: never adopts if the invented household already has items (a user who added before the first import keeps them), and never overrides an explicit activate(). Four regression tests in ActiveHouseholdAdoptionTests.
